epics.title: codebase consistency sweep
epics.description: Fix formatting violations and consolidate structural duplication identified in the May 2026 consistency analysis.
epics.notes: Findings from rt analyze list-smells + find-duplicates sweep on 2026-05-11.

epics.title: SOLID Adherence Analysis
epics.description: Family of rt analyze solid subcommands that detect likely SOLID-principle violations using Roslyn semantic model. One detector per principle; output is JSON grouped by detector name.
epics.notes: P2. Five child stories: SRP, ISP, DIP, OCP, LSP. Each independently shippable.

epics.title: Add structured JSON output to all inspect/analyze commands
epics.description: All rt inspect and rt analyze commands should support --json output so automation consumers (agents, scripts, CI tools) can pipe results without text parsing. Eight commands currently output plain text only.
epics.notes: P2. Affects: find-refs, find-callers, find-undocumented, find-unused, circular-deps, find-magic-strings, list-imports, list-smells. Template: see describe/outline/find-impl which already have JSON output.

epics.title: Platform abstractions: IWorkspaceSessionFactory + ISolutionApplier
epics.description: Introduce injectable abstractions for WorkspaceLoader and SolutionWriter so commands depend on interfaces, not static helpers. Enables testability without AsyncLocal overrides and unblocks daemon workspace caching. Must be a single coordinated change across all ~30 commands.
epics.notes: P2. Architecture gate NoStaticWorkspaceLoaderUse already exists in tests/. rt-006 + rt-007 from issues backlog. Must ship together — splitting doubles the 30-command churn.

epics.title: Consistent command contracts and migration ratchets
epics.description: Make rt commands consistent across handler structure, option vocabulary, metadata, output envelopes, and symbol resolution so dogfooding workflows are predictable and architecture tests can ratchet progress.
epics.notes: From rt dogfooding consistency discussion on 2026-05-15.

userStories.description: As a contributor, I want all source files to pass dotnet format so that CI and editor tooling agree on line endings and encoding.

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: ISP detector — flag fat interfaces and NotImplementedException members
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rt analyze solid --principle ISP to flag over-broad interfaces and implementing classes that throw on members they cannot fulfill.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze solid --principle ISP --solution <sln> exits 0 and emits JSON to stdout
Output has a top-level 'ISP' key with sub-arrays for 'FatInterfaces' and 'UnimplementedMembers'
Each FatInterface item includes: InterfaceName, FilePath, Line, MemberCount
Each UnimplementedMember item includes: TypeName, MemberName, InterfaceName, FilePath, Line
--min-members <N> (default 7) is configurable for the fat-interface threshold
Classes throwing NotImplementedException or NotSupportedException on implemented interface members are flagged under UnimplementedMembers
rt analyze solid --principle all includes ISP results
userStories.notes: P2. Two sub-checks: (1) interfaces with member count above threshold; (2) classes implementing an interface but throwing NotImplementedException/NotSupportedException on one or more members. Output grouped under 'ISP' detector key.

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: DIP detector — flag concrete constructor params and inline new calls
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rt analyze solid --principle DIP to flag high-level classes that depend directly on concrete types rather than abstractions.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze solid --principle DIP --solution <sln> exits 0 and emits JSON to stdout
Output has a top-level 'DIP' key with sub-arrays for 'ConcreteConstructorParams' and 'InlineNewCalls'
Each ConcreteConstructorParam item includes: TypeName, ParamName, ConcreteType, FilePath, Line
Each InlineNewCall item includes: TypeName, MemberName, ConcreteType, FilePath, Line
Value types, record types, and Exception-derived types are excluded from InlineNewCalls
Classes named *Factory, *Builder, or *Provider are excluded from InlineNewCalls (they are expected to new things)
rt analyze solid --principle all includes DIP results
userStories.notes: P2. Two sub-checks: (1) constructors accepting concrete class params (not interfaces/abstract); (2) non-factory class bodies calling new ConcreteType() where ConcreteType is not a value type, DTO, or exception. Output grouped under 'DIP' detector key.

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: OCP detector — flag switch/if chains branching on concrete types
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rt analyze solid --principle OCP to flag code that must be modified every time a new concrete type is added.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze solid --principle OCP --solution <sln> exits 0 and emits JSON to stdout
Output has a top-level 'OCP' key containing an array of violation items
Each item includes: TypeName, MemberName, FilePath, Line, BranchCount, ViolationType ('switch' or 'if-chain')
Flags switch expressions/statements matching on 'is ConcreteType' patterns
Flags if/else chains using 'is ConcreteType' or 'obj.GetType() == typeof(X)' with 2 or more concrete-type branches
--min-branches <N> (default 2) is configurable
rt analyze solid --principle all includes OCP results
userStories.notes: P2. Detects: (1) switch expressions/statements matching on 'is ConcreteType'; (2) if/else chains using 'is ConcreteType' or obj.GetType() == typeof(X) with 2+ branches. Output grouped under 'OCP' detector key.

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: LSP detector — flag overrides throwing or narrowing contracts
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rt analyze solid --principle LSP to flag override methods that break Liskov substitutability so that I can identify types that cannot safely replace their base.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze solid --principle LSP --solution <sln> exits 0 and emits JSON to stdout
Output has a top-level 'LSP' key with sub-arrays for 'ThrowingOverrides' and 'ContractNarrowings'
Each ThrowingOverride item includes: TypeName, MemberName, ExceptionType, FilePath, Line
Each ContractNarrowing item includes: TypeName, MemberName, BaseType, FilePath, Line
Flags override methods whose body contains throw new NotImplementedException() or NotSupportedException()
Flags explicit interface implementations that throw on every code path
rt analyze solid --principle all includes LSP results
userStories.notes: P2. Two sub-checks: (1) override methods whose body throws NotImplementedException/NotSupportedException; (2) explicit interface implementations that throw on every code path. Output grouped under 'LSP' detector key.

userStories.title: rt: convert-static-class — DI registration in Bootstrap.cs
userStories.description: When --no-di-registration is not passed, find a Bootstrap.RegisterServices method in the solution and add a services.Add<Lifetime><ITypeName, TypeName>() line. Discovered during US-027 df pass; command currently warns and skips.

userStories.title: rt: convert-static-class — fix field and ctor formatting in existing-constructor path
userStories.description: When a consumer class already has constructors, AddConstructorInjection inserts the new field without a trailing newline, causing it to merge with the existing first member on the same line. Similarly, AddConstructorParameter inserts parameters without comma spacing and prepends assignments without newlines before the closing brace. dotnet format corrects these cosmetically but they should be emitted correctly. Discovered during US-027 df dry-run.
acceptanceCriteria: When a consumer class already has a constructor, the injected field is inserted on its own line (with correct indentation), not concatenated with the existing first member on the same line
When AddConstructorParameter adds a parameter to an existing constructor, a space follows the preceding comma in the parameter list
When AddConstructorParameter prepends an assignment to the constructor body, the assignment is on its own line before the closing brace
All three fixes apply when multiple constructors are present in the consumer class
Existing tests for add_dependencies_to_existing_instance_constructors remain green
userStories.notes: P2. df dogfood bug. Sibling of the no-constructor formatting bug fixed in the df/convert-static-class-interface-and-di branch commit 1fcf269.

userStories.title: Suppress MSBuild workspace warnings by default; opt in with --show-workspace-warnings
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want MSBuild workspace warnings suppressed by default so that NuGet audit noise and compatibility warnings from the loaded solution don't pollute rt's output.
acceptanceCriteria: All MSBuild workspace warnings are suppressed from stderr by default when rt loads a solution
A --show-workspace-warnings flag (or equivalent) re-enables them for debugging
Genuine solution load errors that prevent rt from running still exit 1 with a clear message
The [workspace-warnings] block does not appear in normal output
userStories.notes: P2. Affects WorkspaceLoader / MSBuildWorkspace diagnostic handling. Suppress all MSBuildWorkspace diagnostics by default; add --show-workspace-warnings global flag to restore them. Genuine load errors (exit 1) must still surface.

userStories.title: Convert solution-not-found crash to clean exit-1 error message
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want a missing solution file to produce a clear error message and exit 1, not an unhandled FileNotFoundException stack trace.
acceptanceCriteria: When the --solution path does not exist, rt prints a single error line to stderr (e.g. 'Error: solution not found: <path>') and exits 1 — no stack trace
The same clean exit-1 pattern applies to any FileNotFoundException thrown during solution loading
The UseExceptionHandler in App.cs (or equivalent top-level handler) catches FileNotFoundException and formats it as a user-facing error
Exit code is 1 (not 0, not unhandled crash code)
No stack trace or 'Unhandled exception:' prefix appears in output
userStories.notes: P1. WorkspaceLoader.cs:84 throws FileNotFoundException; it propagates unhandled through the System.CommandLine pipeline. Catch at the top-level UseExceptionHandler in App.cs (or at the throw site) and emit a single stderr line. No stack trace in normal output.

userStories.title: Catch common exception types in UseExceptionHandler and emit clean exit-1 messages
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want routine exceptions (bad file, bad JSON, not-found) to produce a single clean error line to stderr, not an unhandled exception stack trace.
acceptanceCriteria: UseExceptionHandler in App.cs catches FileNotFoundException, IOException, InvalidOperationException, JsonException, and YamlException and emits a single 'Error: <message>' line to stderr with exit code 1
No stack trace or 'Unhandled exception:' prefix appears for these exception types
Exceptions from DecisionStore.Load/Save (FileNotFoundException, YamlException, IOException) are handled the same way
Exceptions from AddXmlDocCommand JSON file loading are handled the same way
Unexpected exceptions (not in the list above) still surface as unhandled so they are visible during development
userStories.notes: P1. App.cs UseExceptionHandler currently does not catch typed exceptions. Catch: FileNotFoundException, IOException, InvalidOperationException, JsonException, YamlException. Format as 'Error: <ex.Message>' to stderr, exit 1. Covers: WorkspaceLoader throws beyond the missing-solution case (US-041), DecisionStore.Load/Save, AddXmlDocCommand JSON load, MigrateToIOptionsService.

userStories.title: Replace Environment.Exit(1) in OutlineCommand with context.ExitCode = 1
userStories.description: As a developer, I want OutlineCommand to exit consistently with all other commands so that graceful cleanup runs on error.
acceptanceCriteria: OutlineCommand no longer calls Environment.Exit(1) for any error condition
Error cases in OutlineCommand set context.ExitCode = 1 and return, consistent with all other commands
Process exit allows graceful cleanup (log flushing, disposables) to run
userStories.notes: P2. OutlineCommand.cs line ~90 calls Environment.Exit(1). Replace with context.ExitCode = 1; return; — same pattern as every other command in the codebase.

userStories.title: Guard .First()/.Last() calls in SymbolLocator and MethodExtractor against empty sequences
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want empty-sequence edge cases to produce a clear error rather than an InvalidOperationException crash.
acceptanceCriteria: No .First() or .Last() call in SymbolLocator or MethodExtractor throws InvalidOperationException when the sequence is empty
Each call site uses FirstOrDefault with a null check, or validates the collection is non-empty before calling First/Last
When an expected symbol or statement is not found, the command emits a descriptive error to stderr and exits 1 rather than crashing
userStories.notes: P2. SymbolLocator.cs lines ~49, 96, 135, 188 and MethodExtractor.cs lines ~57, 164, 168, 378, 501, 529-532 call .First()/.Last() on sequences that could be empty under certain inputs. Replace with FirstOrDefault + null check or add pre-call validation.

userStories.title: Introduce IWorkspaceSessionFactory + WorkspaceSession (rt-006)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all commands to depend on IWorkspaceSessionFactory instead of calling WorkspaceLoader.LoadAsync directly so that the static coupling is broken and daemon workspace caching becomes possible.
acceptanceCriteria: IWorkspaceSessionFactory interface defined in Core/ with LoadAsync(string? solutionPath) signature
WorkspaceSession : IWorkspaceSessionFactory introduced — instance wrapper delegating to static WorkspaceLoader internals
All ~30 production command handlers accept IWorkspaceSessionFactory, not WorkspaceLoader directly
No command file imports WorkspaceLoader after the change
rt inspect find-refs --symbol WorkspaceLoader --solution RoslynTools.slnx shows 0 production call sites
Architecture gate NoStaticWorkspaceLoaderUse (tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Architecture/) passes
All existing tests pass — WorkspaceLoader.UseOverride pattern updated to stub IWorkspaceSessionFactory
Must ship in same PR as US-054 (ISolutionApplier) — partial rollout is not safe
userStories.notes: P2. Blast radius: 30 production call sites + 100+ test references (WorkspaceLoader.UseOverride). Architecture gate already exists. WorkspaceLoader is static so cannot implement the interface — WorkspaceSession wrapper is the bridge. From issue rt-006.

userStories.title: Introduce ISolutionApplier and update mutation commands (rt-007)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all mutation commands to depend on ISolutionApplier instead of calling SolutionWriter.ApplyChangesAsync directly, bundled with US-053 so the 30-command update happens once.
acceptanceCriteria: ISolutionApplier interface defined: Task ApplyAsync(Solution original, Solution updated, bool dryRun)
SolutionWriter implements ISolutionApplier
All mutation commands accept ISolutionApplier, not SolutionWriter directly
rt inspect find-refs --symbol SolutionWriter --solution RoslynTools.slnx shows 0 production call sites after change
All existing tests pass
Implemented in the same PR as US-053
userStories.notes: P2. 22 fan-in from Commands scope. Must ship with US-053 — splitting doubles the churn across all 30 commands. From issue rt-007.

ChangeSignatureCommand.Build() drops from 76 to ~42 lines after apply
Command file no longer imports WorkspaceLoader or SolutionWriter after apply
Created handler class has signature: static async Task<int> HandleAsync(<RequestType> request)
Lambda body replaced with: context.ExitCode = await <HandlerName>.HandleAsync(new <RequestType>(...))
Using directives in the command file updated to reference the new handler namespace
--dry-run shows diff without writing; without flag, writes files
IRtCommand contract satisfied; command registered under rt refactor group
Test suite passes after apply (no broken imports)

rt inspect find-refs --symbol WorkspaceLoader --json | rt refactor rename --new-name SolutionLoader --dry-run produces the correct diff

userStories.title: Introduce a shared read-only command handler wrapper
userStories.description: As an rt maintainer, I want read-only commands to execute through a shared wrapper so solution loading, timing, cancellation, error mapping, and result rendering are consistent.

The wrapper owns solution loading, cancellation token flow, exception-to-exit-code mapping, and output rendering
At least one representative inspect command and one analyze command are migrated to the wrapper
Migrated command tests cover success, not found, and invalid input paths
An architecture test detects migrated commands that bypass the wrapper

userStories.title: Standardize common CLI options through option factories
userStories.description: As an rt maintainer, I want common options to be created by shared factories so aliases, descriptions, defaults, and required flags do not drift between commands.
acceptanceCriteria: CommandOptionFactory exposes factories for solution, format/json, scope, top, symbol, type, dry-run, and verbose options
Existing migrated commands use the shared factories instead of manually declaring equivalent options
Factory-created options preserve current public CLI behavior unless explicitly documented
Tests assert consistent aliases and descriptions for at least solution, format/json, scope, and top
An architecture test flags manual declarations of common options in migrated command files

userStories.title: Add machine-readable command capabilities to RtCommandInfo

userStories.title: Normalize command outputs around shared result contracts

userStories.title: Create a command migration playbook
userStories.description: As an rt contributor, I want a concise migration playbook so future command refactors follow the same sequence and know which architecture ratchets to update.
acceptanceCriteria: A playbook documents the recommended order: result contract, option factories, handler wrapper, capabilities, symbol query, and ratchet update
The playbook includes a before/after checklist for one migrated command
The playbook explains when to use feedback for missing rt affordances
The playbook lists verification commands including architecture tests and targeted command tests
The playbook is linked from the relevant backlog epic or developer docs
userStories.notes: P3. Keep this short and operational; it should support ongoing dogfooding rather than becoming a design document.

userStories.title: Revisit nested-branch pattern in execute skill for trunk-based repos
userStories.description: As a developer running /execute on a trunk repo, I want a clear consistent policy on RT gap handling, so the skill matches the actual workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: The skill documents a clear policy: nested branches OR fix-on-main for trunk repos — not both
The Opus review section and regression handler are consistent with the chosen policy
The branch cleanup gate is present or removed to match
Risks of fix-on-main are documented (no revert path) if that approach is chosen
userStories.notes: P3. Deferred from 2026-05-15 retro (Proposal 4). Aggressive version in ai-rules commit 8c1a08a; conservative rollback in dae9046. Three places still inconsistent: RT gap section, Opus review section, regression handler. Must be decided and applied consistently.
